title: Fine-tuning Whistle
summary: Teach Whistle a new language or your own vocabulary on your machine: the data, the commands, and what to expect.
body_markdown:
[Whistle](https://huggingface.co/Cactus-Compute/whistle) transcribes seven languages.` needle whistle finetune` adapts it to your speakers and vocabulary, or teaches it a new language, on your own machine.` needle whistle build` turns the result into a` .cact` that the same engine runs.


## Install


```text
pip   install   "cactus-needle[train]"
```


## Data


Three JSONL files, for training, validation and test. Each line is one JSON object: a WAV file, its transcript and its language.


```text
{  "audio"  :   "clips/0001.wav"  ,   "text"  :   "Quero reservar uma mesa para dois."  ,   "language"  :   "pt"  }
```


- ` audio` is relative to the JSONL file. Clips over 30 seconds and empty transcripts are skipped.
- ` language` is a language code. A code Whistle knows adapts that language; any other code adds a new one.
- To keep the other languages as they are, mix some of their clips into the training file.


## New characters


Characters the tokenizer lacks, such as Portuguese ã and õ or any Cyrillic letter, are split into bytes. List the ones your language uses in` tokens.txt` , one per line, and pass it with` --tokens` . Each one becomes a single token.


```text
ã
õ
ç
â
ê
```


## Train and build


```text
needle   whistle   finetune   train.jsonl   validation.jsonl   test.jsonl   --tokens   tokens.txt   --out   adapter.safetensors
needle   whistle   build   --lora   adapter.safetensors   --out   tuned.cact
```


The first run downloads the base checkpoint. Training prints the training and validation loss after each epoch and ends with the word error rate on the test set. That number is a quick greedy decode on the 4-bit weights; for real-world numbers, build the` .cact` and transcribe the test set with it.


The defaults are 3 epochs, batch 16 and learning rate 1e-4. Treat them as a starting point: try a few values of` --epochs` ,` --lr` and` --batch-size` on your data, and keep the run with the lowest validation loss.


` build` merges the adapter and writes a` .cact` that carries your languages and tokens. It is about 29 MB, against 16.9 MB for the shipped model, because local fine-tuning exports at 4 bits instead of 2.


## Run


```text
import   needle


needle.transcribe(  "clip.wav"  ,   weights  =  "tuned.cact"  )
```


Streaming, keywords and word timestamps work as they do with the shipped model.


## How much data


A new language has to learn its tag and its characters, so it needs more steps or a higher learning rate than adapting a language Whistle knows. Brazilian Portuguese from about ten hours of FLEURS, at` --lr 1e-2` with the other defaults, went from 106.2% to 30.5% word error rate on FLEURS test and was detected as Portuguese on every test clip.


Two new languages in one run need enough data each before detection tells them apart. Scripts the base has never seen, such as Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, need far more data before the text is usable.
